inhibition of cyclophilins exerts cardioprotection in reperfused post-infracted hearts of female rats during the acute phase of injury but fails to protect after 4 weeks.

the inhibition of cyclophilins by sanglifehrin-A exerts cardioprotection only during acute post-myocardial infarction injury, and that the cardioprotectiveness of sanglifehrina-A is reperfusion-dependent.

CyP-D is an important regulator of mitochondrial respiration and ROS production in the female post-infarct heart and that its inhibition exerts cardiomyocyte-protective effects in reperfusions but not in nonreperfused infarcts.

the effects of cyclophilins in the heart.
the question of how a drug can be effective in one disease model but not in the other.
the question of whether cyclophilin inhibition is a promising therapeutic target to improve cardiac function after myocardial infarct in women, and the answer is negative.
